# Time Entry and Billing Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Time Entry and Billing Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 20 captured build checkpoints; 5 skills; 2 knowledge files; 5 acceptance checks; 5 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model and keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded billing files, proposed Dynamics 365, SharePoint and Teams connectors, and channels; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who builds, tests and later uses the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for finance records, approval evidence and exception-review connections with dedicated references; the synthetic workshop needs none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare billing, finance, compliance and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview without publishing. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: GitHub Copilot in VS Code Agent mode, the Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Billing-rule ownership | Have finance approve the daily-hours, rate, approval and budget checks coded in the portable agent before auditing real time. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Finance business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Month-end billing review: entries blocked, flagged, held or disputed before invoicing, and how each is found. Agree where manual review misses evidence or overstates invoice readiness before attributing change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Close period | Entries blocked | Audit flags | Fixed-fee holds | Disputes open | Evidence location | Review owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Finance business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Finance business owner | Approve billing scope, control thresholds, escalation and success measures; keep synthetic amounts out of customer results. |
| Billing and finance approvers | Grant consultant, project-manager, billing-manager, milestone and finance approvals where the rules require them; own client contact. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and five skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any finance connection is approved. |
| Finance data and connection owners | Approve Dynamics 365, SharePoint and Teams access; record dedicated connection references and least-privilege identities. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check TEB-01 through TEB-05, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject blocker text or anchors echoed after a grounding failure. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route finance decisions to the approvers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for billing review are agreed.
- [ ] The finance owner records how blocked, flagged, held and disputed work is found today before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/time-entry-billing/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded, with maker access granted, before any build starts.
- [ ] The authenticated finance audience and least-privilege scopes for time, rate, budget and invoice data are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/time-entry-billing/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/time-entry-billing/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/time-entry-billing/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/time-entry-billing/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Time Entry and Billing Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_billing-rules-and-disputes.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_billing-synthetic-ledger.md
8. Add skill: billing-summary
9. Add skill: dispute-resolution
10. Add skill: invoice-preparation
11. Add skill: time-entry-audit
12. Add skill: unbilled-report
13. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
14. Open a fresh Preview conversation
15. Pass TEB-01: Billing Manager
16. Pass TEB-02: Finance Vice President
17. Pass TEB-03: Billing Compliance Lead
18. Pass TEB-04: Billing Manager
19. Pass TEB-05: Client Finance Partner
20. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: TEB-01, TEB-02, TEB-03, TEB-04, TEB-05. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, its smoke test calls `TimeEntryBillingAgent` and returns the required markers.
- [ ] If built manually, the Draft has the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, five skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Unchanged TEB-01 through TEB-05 prompts pass, each in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Each case passes on its grounded final response; blocker text or echoed anchors are not proof.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing time, rate, budget or invoice data. Request only the read scopes the approved finance sources need. Restrict the audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Finance data and connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 — read:** Bind approved read-only connector actions for time, budget and invoice records.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Approve nothing; state the missing description and approval and name the approvers. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a posting, approval, message or invoice succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate SharePoint

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Finance data and connection owners

1. **Bind SharePoint — read:** Add approved SharePoint evidence as a knowledge source with a content owner.

2. **Identity for SharePoint:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope SharePoint:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for SharePoint:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Generate nothing; keep the fixed-fee hold until milestone evidence determines value. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a posting, approval, message or invoice succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Finance data and connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — write:** Gate any posting or approval workflow behind authorized finance review (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Waive nothing and contact no client; brief the evidence gap and internal approval path. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return the evidence and next authorized approver, and end with the no-change statement.

### Step 3-4. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Finance data and connection owners

Bind approved Dynamics 365, SharePoint and Microsoft Teams connections through dedicated references, read-only first.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved Dynamics 365, SharePoint and Teams connections replace the synthetic inputs and preserve the reviewed input and output contract.
- [ ] No posting, approval, message or client contact is claimed unless an approved production tool returns evidence of success.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as finance users and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic limits, rates and budget bands are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked billing corpus | All five cases, TEB-01 through TEB-05, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, five skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Finance authority | Any time change, approval, revenue recognition, posting, invoice, waiver or client contact is no-go. |
| Grounded answers | A response built after the grounding files failed to load cannot pass, even if it repeats the anchors. |
| Release state | The manual and pilot agents are Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Finance business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Finance business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Production publication has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved finance audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review billing sessions, failed interactions, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses an eligible environment type and a supported restore target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
